title: driver-turso: the remote transport's statements are not counted in Server-Timing `db`, so a hosted environment always answers `db;dur=0;desc="0 queries"`
body:
director#1 · hotlong · session_f4c42f815d5e47b39de5e9fb0d6d7864

**① Reproduced defect.** `reach:` hosted staging environment `os-2ph4c1.objectos.app`, 2026-11-15, admin session, `X-OS-Debug-Timing: json`.

Reader: `domain:server` lane, one PR in `packages/drivers/driver-turso`.

## What happens

On a hosted environment, every answer reports zero database work, even when the request plainly reads the database:

| request | status | `db` member | `handler` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/data/sys_user?top=1` | 200 | `db;dur=0;desc="0 queries"` | 367 ms |
| `GET /api/v1/data/sys_user?top=5` | 200 | `db;dur=0;desc="0 queries"` | 503 ms |
| `GET /api/v1/meta/object/sys_user` | 200 | `db;dur=0;desc="0 queries"` | 201 ms |

The admin-only `X-OS-Debug-Timing-Detail` header is absent on all three, because there are no `db` detail samples to report.

## Why

- The `db` member and its detail are fed by `SqlDriver.installQueryTiming()` (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-class-head.ts:500`), which listens on **knex** `query` / `query-response` events.
- In remote mode, `TursoDriver` sends its statements through `RemoteTransport` (`packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts`), which calls `@libsql/client` directly: `this.client.execute(…)` (about 25 sites) and `this.client.batch(…)` (lines 1348, 2193, 2245, 2272, 2723). Knex never sees these statements, so nothing is counted.
- Every hosted environment runs on the remote transport, so the hosted plane has no per-request database timing at all.

## Why it matters

- **cloud#4369, reading 1** (in-container round trip to Turso, owed to the transactions topic #32500) cannot be read today without a one-off probe in the container. With this fixed, an admin request with `X-OS-Debug-Timing: json` gives per-statement durations measured inside the container, which is exactly that reading.
- Hosted performance work (cloud#2914, cloud#3103) has had to infer database time from `handler` totals.

## Expected

- Each `execute` and each `batch` round trip in `RemoteTransport` is counted into the ambient collector: `countServerTiming('db', dur, 'queries')`, the same mark `driver-sql` produces.
- When detail capture is on, it records the parametrized SQL shape (for a batch, one sample per round trip, labelled e.g. `batch(<n>): <first statement shape>`). Bindings are never recorded.
- Simplest seam: one private helper wrapping `client.execute` / `client.batch`, used at every call site, or a wrapper installed where `ensureConnected()` creates the client.

## Acceptance

- A unit test in `driver-turso` with a stubbed client and an active `PerfTiming`: one `execute` and one `batch` give `db` count 2, and detail samples carry SQL shapes without bindings.
- After the pin reaches staging: the three requests above report a non-zero `db` count, and `X-OS-Debug-Timing: json` from an admin returns `X-OS-Debug-Timing-Detail`.

## Not in scope

- No change to the disclosure gate (admin-only per request, global mode via `OS_SERVER_TIMING`).
- No change to transactions (#32500 stays on hold).

Dedupe:
- `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack "Server-Timing" turso` → 14 hits;
- `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack RemoteTransport timing` → 11 hits;
- `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack Server-Timing db remote` → 14 hits (open and closed).

The closest is #32500 (the transactions topic, which needs the reading, not this fix). #24523 (closed) is about an extra authz read, not the timing seam. None covers the remote transport missing from `db` timing.

Related: cloud#4369, #32500.
